name: Curriculum Map

panels.map:
How the series maps to the Red Seal Industrial Mechanic (Millwright) occupational standard
The Red Seal Occupational Standard organises the trade into major work activities, each broken into tasks and sub-tasks. BuiltWright's modules were written to the field practice, not to the standard, so the map below is by area rather than by task number. It is intended to help a training coordinator or a college instructor see what the series covers and where it fits alongside the apprenticeship curriculum, and to help an apprentice preparing for the interprovincial exam find the module for a topic. Task and sub-task numbers should be taken from the current edition of the standard, which is revised periodically. The series is a supplement to trade school and on-the-job training, not a replacement for either.
Standard area (major work activity)BuiltWright modulesDepth
Common occupational skills: safety, hazard identification, lockout, documentation, tools, measuring, communicationEvery Safety tab; 14 Safeguarding and PSR; 21 Precision Measurement; 16 Root Cause; 12 ReferenceStrong on lockout, hazard identification, measurement, and documentation. Rigging is in RigIt.
Rigging, hoisting, and liftingReferenced from 09, 10, 13, 15 Safety tabs; full coverage in RigItAwareness only in this series.
Fabrication, machining, welding, and cutting14 Safeguarding (guard construction); 21 Precision MeasurementLight. Welding fundamentals is a planned module.
Prime movers: electric motors, engines, turbines10 Motors (mechanical side); 18 Compressors (drives)Strong on motors as mechanical machines and the electrical handoff. Engines and turbines not covered.
Power transmission: couplings, alignment, bearings, seals, belts, chains, gearboxes, clutches, brakes, lubrication02 Bearings; 03 Couplings and Alignment; 04 Seals and Gaskets; 05 Lubrication; 08 Power Transmission; 09 Gearboxes; 19 Clutches and Brakes; 11 VibrationThe core of the series. Comprehensive.
Fluid power: hydraulics and pneumatics06 Pneumatics; 07 Hydraulics; 20 Process Valves (actuators)Comprehensive on systems, components, symbols, troubleshooting, and safety.
Process equipment: pumps, compressors, fans, blowers, valves, mixers, tanks01 Pumps; 17 Fans and Blowers; 18 Compressors; 20 Process ValvesStrong on pumps, fans, compressors, and valves. Mixers and agitators not covered as a module.
Material handling: conveyors, elevators, hoists15 Conveyors; 19 Clutches and Brakes (holding brakes, backstops)Strong on belt conveyors; other conveyor types at overview depth.
Installation, foundations, and commissioning13 Installation and Foundations; 03 Alignment; 11 Vibration (baselines)Comprehensive.
Maintenance systems: preventive maintenance, condition monitoring, failure analysisPM Task Library; 11 Vibration; 05 Lubrication (oil analysis); 16 Root CauseStrong. The PM library is derived from every diagnostic result.
Machine safeguarding and regulatory compliance (Ontario)14 Safeguarding and PSR; Reference (Standards Cited)Comprehensive for Ontario; the regulatory content is Ontario-specific.
Not yet covered, for completeness
  • Welding fundamentals and metallurgy (planned).
  • Rigging and hoisting (RigIt, a separate Hatt Industrial Trades product).
  • Fasteners and joining in depth (ButtonUp, a separate product; the Reference module has torque basics).
  • Engines, turbines, and steam systems.
  • Mixers, agitators, and vessels.
  • Machining and layout beyond measurement.
  • Blueprint and drawing reading beyond fluid power symbols (TradeLens, a separate product in development).
panels.levels:
The same modules read at three levels
LearnerUse the module forWhich tabsMeasure of progress
First and second year apprenticeVocabulary, how things work, what the parts are called, why the rules existOverview, types and anatomy tabs, Safety, Self-CheckSelf-check sections answered with the reasons read; can explain a component to a journeyman
Third and fourth year apprentice, new journeypersonDiagnosis, procedures, the numbers, reading failed partsTroubleshoot trees, installation and setup tabs, Reference tables, Root CauseWalks a fault through a tree and arrives at the right result before being told; uses the reference tables without prompting
Experienced journeyperson, lead hand, maintenance supervisorTraining others, writing PMs, root cause, PSR homework, choosing the fix at the right levelPrevent-recurrence tails, PM Task Library, Root Cause report, Safeguarding PSR tab, Manager's GuideRepeat failure rate falls on the machines they own; PM sheets carry quantities and settings; root cause reports reach a system cause
A module is not read once. An apprentice reads the overview of the bearing module in year one, works the troubleshoot tree in year three, and writes the PM from it as a lead hand. The self-check and the trees are built so that the same page pays off at each stage.
panels.paths:
Learning paths by role and by machine
By role
PathOrderWhy this order
New maintenance technician onboarding (12 weeks)14 Safeguarding; 21 Measurement; 02 Bearings; 05 Lubrication; 03 Alignment; 08 Power Transmission; 01 Pumps; 06 Pneumatics; 10 Motors; 09 Gearboxes; 15 Conveyors; 16 Root CauseSafety and measurement first because everything depends on them; then the components that fail most; then the machines built from them; then the thinking skill. The Manager's Guide has the week-by-week version.
Rotating equipment specialist02, 03, 11, 05, 09, 13, 01, 17, 10, 16Bearings, alignment, and vibration are the core; installation prevents the faults; pumps, fans, and motors are the machines.
Fluid power specialist06, 07, 20, 18, 05, 04Pneumatics before hydraulics (same logic, lower stakes); valves and compressors are the applications; lubrication and seals are the failure modes.
Maintenance planner or supervisor16 Root Cause; PM Task Library; 14 Safeguarding; 13 Installation; then the Overview and Safety tabs of every moduleThe planner needs the causes, the tasks, the compliance, and enough of every subject to ask good questions.
Interprovincial exam preparationAll Self-Check tabs, then the Reference module, then the troubleshoot trees of the modules where the self-check was weakestThe self-checks are written at the level of the exam's practical judgment questions.
By machine
MachineModules, in the order the faults come
Centrifugal pump set01 Pumps; 04 Seals; 03 Alignment; 02 Bearings; 05 Lubrication; 10 Motors; 13 Installation; 11 Vibration
Belt conveyor15 Conveyors; 08 Power Transmission; 09 Gearboxes (shaft mount); 19 Clutches and Brakes (backstop); 02 Bearings; 14 Safeguarding (nip points)
Packaging or assembly machine06 Pneumatics; 14 Safeguarding; 19 Clutches and Brakes; 08 Power Transmission; 10 Motors; 20 Process Valves (actuators)
Hydraulic press07 Hydraulics; 14 Safeguarding (light curtains, two-hand, stop time); 19 Clutches and Brakes (clutch-brake units); 05 Lubrication
Compressed air system18 Compressors; 06 Pneumatics (air quality, leaks); 20 Process Valves (relief); 17 Fans (cooling)
HVAC or process fan17 Fans; 08 Power Transmission; 02 Bearings; 11 Vibration; 10 Motors
Overhead crane or hoist19 Clutches and Brakes (holding brakes); 09 Gearboxes; 10 Motors; 14 Safeguarding; RigIt

css: .bw-tab { font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace; font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 1px; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 4px; border: 0.5px solid #3a3a36; background: #242420; color: #888780; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s; text-transform: uppercase; }
.family-label { font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace; font-size: 9px; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #BA7517; text-transform: uppercase; margin: 1rem 0 0.5rem 0; }
.type-card { background: #2e2e2a; border: 1px solid #3a3a36; border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.9rem; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s; }
.comp-detail { background: #2e2e2a; border: 0.5px solid #3a3a36; border-radius: 8px; padding: 1.25rem; margin-bottom: 1.25rem; }
.comp-detail-tips li::before { content: '→'; position: absolute; left: 0; color: #BA7517; }
.callout-tips li { font-size: 13px; color: #888780; padding: 3px 0 3px 16px; position: relative; line-height: 1.5; }
.callout-tips li::before { content: '→'; position: absolute; left: 0; color: #EF9F27; }
.adv-wrap { border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden; border: 0.5px solid #3a3a36; margin-bottom: 1.25rem; }
.adv-toggle { width: 100%; background: #242420; border: none; padding: 0.75rem 1.1rem; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; cursor: pointer; gap: 10px; }
.adv-toggle-label { font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace; font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 1.5px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #BA7517; font-weight: 600; text-align: left; }
.adv-body { display: none; background: #1e1e1c; padding: 1rem 1.1rem; border-top: 0.5px solid #3a3a36; }
.chain-wrap { background: #242420; border: 0.5px solid #3a3a36; border-radius: 8px; padding: 1.25rem; margin-bottom: 1.25rem; overflow-x: auto; }
.chain { display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: nowrap; gap: 0; }
.chain-box { background: #2e2e2a; border: 1px solid #3a3a36; border-radius: 6px; padding: 7px 9px; text-align: center; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s; min-width: 70px; }

.sym-card { background: #2e2e2a; border: 1px solid #3a3a36; border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.9rem; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.15s; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 8px; }
.sym-detail { background: #2e2e2a; border: 0.5px solid #3a3a36; border-radius: 8px; padding: 1.25rem; margin-bottom: 1.25rem; }
.sym-detail-tips li { font-size: 12px; color: #888780; padding: 2px 0 2px 16px; position: relative; line-height: 1.5; }
.sym-detail-tips li::before { content: '→'; position: absolute; left: 0; color: #BA7517; font-size: 11px; }

.ref-table th { font-family: 'Share Tech Mono', monospace; font-size: 9px; letter-spacing: 1px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #BA7517; text-align: left; padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid #3a3a36; }
.ref-table td { padding: 6px 8px; border-bottom: 0.5px solid #2e2e2a; color: #c8c6bf; vertical-align: top; line-height: 1.4; }
.progress-bar { height: 3px; background: #242420; border-radius: 2px; margin-bottom: 1rem; overflow: hidden; }
.tree-q-hint { font-size: 12px; color: #888780; margin-bottom: 0.75rem; font-style: italic; line-height: 1.45; }

.tree-btn { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.5px; padding: 7px 16px; border-radius: 5px; border: 0.5px solid #3a3a36; background: #242420; color: #e8e6df; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.12s; text-align: left; }

@media print { body { background:#fff; color:#000; padding:0; } .bw-tabs, .ref-search, .tree-back, .sc-score, .adv-chevron, .bw-badge { display:none !important; } .bw-panel { display:none; } .bw-panel.active { display:block; } .bw-wrap { max-width:100%; } .bw-title, .comp-detail-name, .info-block-title, .type-card-name, .sym-card-label, .tree-q-text, .tree-result-text, .route-title, .sc-stem, .callout-box-title, .field-tip strong, .tree-prevent strong, .bw-section-label, .family-label, .ref-table th { color:#000 !important; } .comp-detail-body, .info-block-body, .callout-box-body, .tree-result-sub, .tree-prevent, .field-tip div, .sc-why, .ref-table td, .comp-detail-tips li, .info-block-tips li, .callout-tips li, .sym-detail-body, .adv-body p, .route-text, .type-card-sub, .sym-card-sub, .tree-q-hint, .ref-note, .chain-label, .chain-sub { color:#222 !important; } .comp-detail, .info-block, .callout-box, .type-card, .sym-card, .tree-q, .tree-result, .field-tip, .adv-wrap, .adv-body, .adv-toggle, .chain-wrap, .chain-box, .sc-q, .sym-detail, .calc, .route, .dir-row, .safety-strip { background:#fff !important; border-color:#999 !important; box-shadow:none !important; } .adv-body { display:block !important; } .tree-btn, .sc-opt, .pm-btn { border:0.5px solid #999; background:#fff; color:#000; } .progress-bar { display:none; } a { color:#000; text-decoration:none; } .bw-logo a::after { content:" builtwrightapp.com"; color:#666; } .bw-header { border-bottom:1px solid #000; } .comp-detail, .info-block, .callout-box, .tree-q, .sc-q { page-break-inside: avoid; } }
